Circuits

No circuits yet.

Route

How many relays your traffic passes through, and where they are.

Multi-hop

3

Three hops is Tor's own design and what almost everyone uses. Extra hops cost latency and buy little against an adversary who can already watch both ends. Pinning a country narrows the set of relays you can be assigned, which makes you easier to tell apart from other users — it is a trade, not a free upgrade.

Entry relay

not set

Tor reuses one entry relay for a long time on purpose. Picking a fresh one for every circuit means eventually picking a hostile one, and every change is another chance to be profiled. TorVeil keeps the same guard and only re-rolls it when you clear it here.

Traffic shaping

Making the shape of your traffic tell an observer less about what you are doing.

Profile

Cover traffic ceiling

KiB/s — 0 uses the profile default

Cover traffic is sent to an onion service this application hosts, so the dummy bytes never reach an exit relay or the wider internet — but they still travel about six relay hops each way, and that bandwidth is donated by volunteers. Raise this only if you need it.

What this does and does not do

Shaping aligns every outbound write to a shared clock, turns on Tor's own link and circuit padding at full strength, and mixes cover traffic into the same connection as your real traffic. Together that blunts the timing and volume patterns a website-fingerprinting classifier feeds on.

It protects against someone watching the link between you and your entry relay — an ISP or a network operator. It hides nothing from the exit relay, which still sees where your traffic goes, and it is not a defence against an adversary who can watch both ends of a circuit at the same time.

Settings

Changing anything here needs a reconnect.

Mode

Transport

The Tor Project rotates these; copy current ones from Tor Browser if they stop working.

Tunnel

Tor carries TCP only. UDP, QUIC and ICMP cannot be tunnelled, so QUIC is blocked to make browsers fall back to TCP, and IPv6 is blocked because it would otherwise reach the internet straight past the tunnel. Full-tunnel mode needs administrator rights.

Local listeners

Loopback addresses only. Binding these to a routable address would make this machine an open proxy.

Tor installation

TorVeil does not bundle Tor: it drives a Tor build you install, so the binary you run stays one you can verify. Install the Tor Expert Bundle or Tor Browser, or point this at a folder containing tor.exe.

Log

Kept in memory only and never written to disk. Closing TorVeil discards it.
